styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Forbidden City, Great Wall and the Temple of Heaven.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Peking duck, dumplings and hutong snacks.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Hutongs, temples, markets and the 798 art district.

stays.why: Walk to Tiananmen and the Forbidden City; quiet hutongs nearby for dinner.
Best for bars, restaurants and shopping; easy metro and taxi links.
Lakeside hutongs, close to the Drum Tower and Beihai Park.
Central shopping street, one metro stop from the Forbidden City.

food: Try Peking duck at a roast-duck restaurant; book ahead for dinner and expect roughly ¥150–350 per person.
Hutong snacks: jianbing (savoury crepe), baozi and noodles; small shops often cost ¥10–30 a dish.
Look for dumpling houses and noodle shops near your hotel; menus with pictures help if you don't read Chinese.
Street food is best in busy, well-trafficked spots; drink bottled water and skip lukewarm dishes.
Tea houses and courtyard cafés are good for a rest; check prices before ordering in tourist areas.
more_time: Add a full day for the Great Wall: Mutianyu is popular and less crowded than Badaling; go early and check transport on the day.
Spend a morning at the Temple of Heaven and a park to watch locals dance and play cards.
Art and design fans can swap a shopping afternoon for the 798 art district.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the Forbidden City, a Great Wall day and a hutong evening without rushing.

month_notes: Coldest month: highs near 3°C, lows around -7°C. Pack a heavy coat, hat and gloves.
Still cold, highs near 6°C and lows around -5°C. Few rainy days; layer up.
Warming up: highs near 15°C, lows around 1°C. Good for walking the Wall.
Pleasant spring: highs near 22°C, lows around 8°C. Light jacket for evenings.
Warm and dry: highs near 28°C, lows around 14°C. Great sightseeing weather.
Hot: highs near 33°C, lows around 20°C. Start early and rest at midday.
Hottest and wettest: highs near 32°C, about 14 rain days. Carry an umbrella.
Hot and humid: highs near 30°C, about 12 rain days. Stay hydrated.
Cooling down: highs near 27°C, lows around 16°C. One of the best months.
Mild and clear: highs near 19°C, lows around 8°C. Ideal for the Great Wall.
Cool: highs near 10°C, lows around 0°C. Warm layers needed.
Cold again: highs near 3°C, lows around -6°C. Few rainy days; dress warmly.

climate_guide.summary: Four clear seasons: cold, dry winters and hot, rainy summers. Spring and autumn are the best times to visit.

items.title: Best time: April, May, September, October
items.text: Highs around 19–28°C with low rain. Perfect for the Great Wall and long walks.

items.title: Winter is cold and dry
items.text: December to February highs near 3–6°C and lows below freezing. Very little rain; pack a heavy coat.

items.title: Summer is hot and wet
items.text: June to August highs near 30–33°C, with the most rain in July. Plan indoor sights at midday.

items.title: Rain peaks in July and August
items.text: About 12–14 rain days a month then. Other months are mostly dry.

items.title: Spring can be windy and dusty
items.text: March and April bring wind; air quality varies. Check the day's forecast before outdoor plans.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers for spring and autumn, a heavy coat for winter, light breathable clothes and an umbrella for summer. Comfortable shoes for long walks.

transit.best: Metro for most trips; DiDi or Alipay taxis for late nights and places off the metro.

modes.text: Extensive, cheap (¥3–10) and reaches most sights. Buy a Yikatong card or use Alipay/WeChat.
Frequent but hard to navigate without Chinese; fares around ¥2.
Metered taxis, but drivers rarely speak English; show place names in Chinese characters. DiDi works and can be paid via Alipay or WeChat; Alipay also books taxis in English.
Needs a Chinese licence and a Beijing entry permit (进京证); most visitors skip driving.
Good in hutongs and parks. Use Baidu or Amap maps, not Google.
Dockless shared bikes are great for last-mile trips; use Baidu or Amap maps.
